subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equation of the tangent and the normal to the curve y⁴ = ax³ at (a, a).

mark_split.label: Check the point and differentiate implicitly
Slope of the tangent at (a, a)

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.222, chapter 10 APPLICATIONS OF DERIVATIVES, the TANGENTS AND NORMALS sub-section, Short Answer question 11(iii). Chapter 10 is printed as five un-numbered sub-sections inside one chapter box and each sub-section restarts its own numbering, so the sub-section is named here; we ship the whole chapter as ONE unit. ONLY THE QUESTION WAS TAKEN — the solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work, see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a CHAPTER-level marks banner (4M over this sub-section) but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split follows the shape this bank uses for a Maths-1B Section B question. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty — the chapter has long been examined, we simply have no sourced years for this question. Paper position: Maths-1B Section B runs Q11 to Q18 at 4 marks each, answer any 6 of 8, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. One further note on the stem: the printed question does not state a ≠ 0. The working here says so, because at a = 0 the curve is y⁴ = 0 and the point (a, a) is the origin, where the slope 3ax²/(4y³) is not defined. Nothing was changed in the question itself.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how you differentiate y⁴ = ax³, what the slope works out to at (a, a), and what happens to the letter a in the answer.

steps.label: Check the point and differentiate implicitly
steps.margin_note: First mark. The dy/dx factor on the left is what the examiner looks for. Without it the line differentiates the wrong equation and every later mark follows the error.
lines: LHS = a⁴   and   RHS = a(a³) = a⁴,
so (a, a) lies on the curve for every value of a.
y is not given in terms of x, so differentiate both sides with respect to x.
The chain rule attaches dy/dx to y⁴:

recall.must_convey: That both sides are differentiated with respect to x, giving 4y³(dy/dx) = 3ax².
accept: differentiate both sides with respect to x
y to the fourth gives four y cubed times dy by dx
a is a constant so a x cubed gives three a x squared
implicit differentiation cheyyali, dy by dx attach avuthundi
check first that a to the fourth equals a times a cubed
four y cubed dy by dx equals three a x squared

steps.why: y is not written in terms of x, so implicit differentiation is the shortest route. Taking a fourth root first would give y = (ax³)¹⁄⁴ and a much longer differentiation for the same slope.
common_mistakes: Differentiating y⁴ to 4y³ and omitting the dy/dx factor.
Treating a as a variable and using the product rule on ax³.
Differentiating with respect to y on one side and x on the other.
steps.memory_tip: Every time a y is differentiated with respect to x, a dy/dx is attached to it. The x terms get nothing extra.

steps.label: Slope of the tangent at (a, a)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Substitute BOTH x = a and y = a. All three a's cancel and m = 3/4 — a plain number, with no a left in it.
lines: At the point (a, a), put x = a and y = a:

recall.must_convey: That substituting x = a and y = a makes the a's cancel and gives m = 3/4.
accept: substitute x equal to a and y equal to a
a cubed cancels top and bottom
the slope of the tangent is three by four
a cubed cancel avuthundi, three by four vasthundi
the slope has no a left in it
m is three quarters

steps.why: a³ cancels between numerator and denominator, so the slope is a pure number: the tangent has the same direction whatever the size of a. That cancelling is the check that the substitution was done correctly.
common_mistakes: Cancelling only one a and leaving m = 3a/4.
Substituting x = a but leaving y in the answer.
Writing m = 4/3, which is the reciprocal and belongs to the normal.
steps.memory_tip: Both coordinates of the point are a, so every a in dy/dx becomes the same letter and cancels. A pure number is the expected result.

steps.label: Equation of the tangent
steps.margin_note: Third mark. a stays in the equation of the line even though it has left the slope — the point (a, a) still depends on it. Check: 3a − 4a + a = 0.
lines: Tangent at (x₁, y₁) with slope m:   y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)

recall.must_convey: That the point-slope form with (a, a) and m = 3/4 gives 3x − 4y + a = 0.
accept: use y minus a equals three by four into x minus a
multiply both sides by four to clear the fraction
the tangent is three x minus four y plus a equals zero
point a comma a tho point slope form rasta
four y minus four a equals three x minus three a
the letter a stays in the line but not in the slope

steps.why: The slope no longer contains a, but the point does, so the line's constant term carries the a. Collecting −4a + 3a to a single +a is where the a survives.
common_mistakes: Dropping a altogether because it cancelled in the slope.
Multiplying only the left side by 4.
steps.memory_tip: a cancelled in the slope but not in the point, so expect exactly one a in the final line.

steps.label: Equation of the normal
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. The normal's slope is −1/m = −4/3, so the reciprocal AND the sign both change. Check at (a, a): 4a + 3a − 7a = 0.
lines: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent at the same point,

recall.must_convey: That the normal's slope is −4/3, giving 4x + 3y − 7a = 0.
accept: the normal slope is minus four by three
turn three by four over and change the sign
the normal is four x plus three y minus seven a equals zero
minus one by m ante minus four by three
three a plus four a gives seven a on the right
the normal passes through a comma a as well

steps.why: The normal's slope is the negative reciprocal of 3/4. The constant term collects −3a and −4a into −7a, which is the arithmetic step most often slipped here.
common_mistakes: Writing the normal's slope as 4/3, inverting without the sign change.
Collecting the a terms to −a instead of −7a.
Using the tangent's slope 3/4 in the normal by copying the previous line.
steps.memory_tip: Tangent slope 3/4 turns over to 4/3 and the sign changes to minus. The two lines then have slopes whose product is −1.

insider_note: Differentiate implicitly; the point (a, a) lies on the curve for EVERY a, which is worth checking first. The a's then cancel, leaving a numerical slope of 3/4.
